To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
androgen‐independant prostate cancer is induced by DMAB in the anterior prostate, but not in the ventral or dorsal lobes of the rat prostate.
androgen‐independence in prostate cancer may be acquired by a multistage process, and that the development of invasive carcinoma is independent of androgen.
androgen‐dependent androgen‐independence carcinomas can be induced in the male accessory sex organs of rats by the combined treatment of DMAB and testosterone propionate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the development of carcinomas in the prostate complex of rats treated with DMAB and/or testosterone propionate.
the development of androgen‐independence in carcinomas arising from androgen‐dependent preneoplastic lesions in rat accessory sex organs.
the induction and development of two different kinds of cancers in rat male accessory organs, one a benign non‐invasive adenocarcinoma and the other an androgen‐independence invasive adenocarcinomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the development of carcinomas of the rat prostate is androgen‐dependent.

in the prostate complex of rats, precancerous lesions and non‐invasive cancers of the ventral lobar epithelium are androgen‐sensitive, while invasive carcinoma of the dorsolateral lobe and the seminal vesicle is androgen‐in‐sensitive.
in the rat prostate, the development of non‐invasice carcinomas is dependent on the presence of androgen, but that of invasive carcinomas is not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
androgen‐dependent non‐invasive cancerous lesions can be transformed into androgen‐independence in the male accessory sex organs of rats.
in the prostate complex, androgen‐dependent carcinogenesis can be induced by DMAB and that androgen‐independence of carcinomas develops from androgen‐dependence of precancerous lesions.
androgen dependence in the ventral prostatic carcinoma may reflect the androgen dependence in its precancerous lesions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
androgens play a critical role in prostate cancer development.
the androgen dependence or independence of carcinomas in the prostate complex is not uniform and depends on the type of cancer.

the prostate cancer is androgen‐dependent in the ventral and anterior lobes, but androgen‐independence is acquired by invasive carcinomas in the dorsolatera and anterior lobes and in the seminal vesicles.
